svg.title: How the stones were worn
svg.desc: A drawn plate of the high priest from the front, without a face, wearing the garments of Exodus 28 numbered in the order Leviticus 8:7-9 puts them on: 1. The coat: Fine linen, woven in checker work (Exodus 28:39). Put on first (Leviticus 8:7). 2. The sash: Embroidered (28:39), tied round the coat (Leviticus 8:7). The robe covers it. 3. The robe of the ephod: All of blue, with an opening for the head; pomegranates and gold bells round the hem, “its sound shall be heard” (28:31-35). Its length is not stated. 4. The ephod: Gold, blue, purple and scarlet in fine linen (28:6): two shoulder pieces and a woven band of one piece with it, tied round him (28:7-8; Leviticus 8:7). The body’s shape is not stated: Rashi makes it an apron worn behind, to the heels (on 28:6); Josephus a short sleeved coat (Antiquities 3.162). 5. Two onyx stones: On the shoulder pieces, six names on each, in birth order: “stones of remembrance” (28:9-12). 6. The breastpiece of judgment: A span square, doubled; twelve stones in four rows (28:15-21). It hangs from the shoulder stones’ settings by gold chains and is tied to the ephod with blue lace (28:22-28). The Urim and Thummim go in it (28:30). 7. The turban and the plate: Fine linen; on its front a gold plate engraved “Holy to the LORD”, on a blue cord (28:36-39). Put on last (Leviticus 8:9). Below, how the breastpiece hangs, drawn at one span square with its twelve stones: A. Two gold rings on the breastpiece’s top corners (28:23). B. Two chains of pure gold, twisted like cords, from those rings to the settings of the shoulder stones (28:14, 24-25). The breastpiece hangs from the stones that carry the names. C. Two more rings on its lower corners, on the inside edge next to the ephod (28:26). D. Two rings on the shoulder pieces, low in front, just above the woven band (28:27). E. A lace of blue ties C to D, “so that it may lie on the skillfully woven band of the ephod, so that the breastpiece shall not come loose” (28:28, ESV). A scale bar marks one span, about 22 cm if a span is half a cubit of 44.5 cm. A small diagram shows a cloth two spans long folded to one span square, making a pocket for the Urim and Thummim, marked as a guess: the text says only that it was doubled and that they were put in it. Solid lines are what the text states; dashed lines are a tradition or a guess. The plate closes with Exodus 28:29.

leave each row at most about 5.5 cm, setting included.
“So Aaron shall bear the names of the sons of Israel in the breastpiece of
judgment on his heart, when he goes into the Holy Place …”
